reader.decision: Present `cache: pnpm` on `actions/setup-node@v4` as the proposal to the team, and mention the explicit `actions/cache` version as a fallback alternative. Before presenting, verify that the real repo has `pnpm-lock.yaml` and that the cache is saved on the default branch.
reader.decision_reason: The message states it is a one-line change that needs no new step or hand-written key, and the explicit version only becomes primary if lockfile changes are frequent, which the message does not say they are. The 35 s figure is not confirmed to include restore time, so I will present the saving as slightly lower than stated.

reconstruction.problem: Each `ci` run does `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` with an empty pnpm store, downloading 1.1 GB and taking a median of 3 min 40 s. Nothing is broken; it is a speed and cost opportunity.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Nothing is broken. The cost is waiting: runs take a median of 11 min 05 s, and merges depend on `ci`. Across 412 runs per week that is about 21 hours of waiting and about 10 USD of runner time.
reconstruction.fix: Add `cache: pnpm` under `with` on `actions/setup-node@v4` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. `pnpm/action-setup@v4` already runs before it. The alternative is `actions/cache` with an explicit store path, key and `restore-keys`.
reconstruction.cost: The `cache: pnpm` version costs one line plus cache storage: 1.1 GB per entry against a 10 GB repository limit, about 9 entries, evicted least-recently-used first. A lockfile change misses the cache once and pays the full 3 min 40 s. The explicit `actions/cache` version costs about 6 more lines in `ci.yml`. The 35 s figure comes from 20 manual warm-store runs and may exclude restore time, so the real saving is slightly lower.

follow_up_questions: Does the real `fernway-web` repository contain `pnpm-lock.yaml`? The snapshot does not, and `cache: pnpm` requires it.
Does `ci` run on the default branch so the cache is saved there and feature branches can read it?
How often does `pnpm-lock.yaml` change per week? This decides whether the explicit `actions/cache` version should be the primary.
reader.closing_answer: I show the team `cache: pnpm` as the proposal, with the explicit `actions/cache` version as the named fallback if lockfile changes turn out to be frequent. I present the saving as slightly under 185 s per run until the restore time is measured.
